title: Reported speech and indirect questions
point: Pass on what someone said with said/told/asked, and soften questions by tucking them inside "Do you know…" or "I wonder…" with normal word order.

sentences.ja: 駅ってどこにあるか分かりますか？
sentences.text: Do you know where the station is?
sentences.note: After "Do you know", the question goes back to statement order: "where the station is", not "where is the station".

sentences.ja: 先生、来週は休講だって言ってたよ。
sentences.text: The professor said there's no class next week.
sentences.note: When the news is still true, native speakers often keep the present tense after "said".

sentences.ja: 彼女に、遅れるって伝えておいてくれる？
sentences.text: Could you tell her I'm running a bit late?

sentences.ja: 店員さんに、席が空いてるか聞いてみるね。
sentences.text: I'll ask the server if they have a table free.

sentences.ja: あの店、まだ開いてるかなあ。
sentences.text: I wonder if that place is still open.
sentences.note: "I wonder if…" is how English says "〜かなあ" when you're thinking out loud.

sentences.ja: このデータを使っていいのかどうか、よく分からないんです。
sentences.text: I'm not sure whether we're allowed to use this data.

sentences.ja: 上司に、報告書はもう終わったのかって聞かれた。
sentences.text: My boss asked me if I'd finished the report yet.

sentences.ja: 何時に始まるか教えてもらえますか？
sentences.text: Could you tell me what time it starts?

sentences.ja: 彼、そのパーティーには行かないって言ってたけど。
sentences.text: He told me he wasn't going to the party, though.
sentences.note: "Told" needs a person after it (told me); "said" doesn't (said that…).

sentences.ja: なんで彼があんなに怒ってたのか、いまだに分からない。
sentences.text: I still don't get why he was so upset.
